title: Visit the Permit Services Center before you sign a lease
summary: The City strongly encourages visiting the Permit Services Center before signing a lease, to learn the space's history and what improvements or permits it will need.
issuer: City of Glendale – Permit Services Center
applies_because: You are opening at a commercial location

title: Confirm your business type is allowed at the address
summary: Certain business types cannot operate in certain zones. Check the Glendale Zoning and Parcel Map before applying. A Business Registration Certificate does not authorize a change of use.
applies_because: You are opening at a commercial location

title: Business Registration Certificate (BRC) required
summary: Every business located in Glendale, including subleases, must hold a valid BRC, renewed annually and posted visibly. Any change in activities, square footage, name, ownership or address requires a new BRC.
issuer: City of Glendale – Community Development, Neighborhood Services
applies_because: Your business is located in Glendale (not home-based)

title: BRC fee, documents and renewal
summary: Initial fee $496.39; annual renewal $128.77. Apply or renew through the GlendalePermits online portal with one of: a signed lease showing the property address, the grant deed, or the secured annual property tax bill. Subleases need a signed sublease agreement (and an owner letter if the owner is not listed on it). If the BRC is not obtained within 180 days of paying, the application is considered withdrawn. Renewal opens 30 days before expiration; if not renewed before expiration, a new BRC application is required.
issuer: City of Glendale – Community Development, Neighborhood Services
documents: Lease, grant deed, or secured property tax bill; GlendalePermits account
apply_url: GlendalePermits portal (copy the exact URL from the City page)
deadlines: Obtain the certificate within 180 days of paying the application fee
Renew every year; renewal opens 30 days before expiration
applies_because: Your business is located in Glendale (not home-based)

title: Home-based business: Home Occupation Permit (not a BRC)
summary: Home businesses apply for a Home Occupation Permit through GlendalePermits instead of a BRC. You must live there; no signs (including on the mailbox); no employees working on the property; the activity must fit a residential neighborhood.
apply_url: GlendalePermits portal (copy the exact URL from the City page)
applies_because: You run the business from where you live

title: Home occupation size limit
summary: A home occupation generally may not occupy more than 10% of the dwelling's floor area (with exceptions, including California Homemade Food Act uses).
applies_because: You run the business from where you live

title: Public Health Permit for food facilities (LA County)
summary: New food facilities need LA County Environmental Health approval of design and construction through the plan check process before a Public Health Permit is issued. If you are buying an existing restaurant with no major construction, contact the nearest Environmental Health district office. Do not send payment until you receive an invoice from Public Health.
issuer: LA County Department of Public Health – Environmental Health
fee: See the County fee schedule (not stated here)
documents: Plans for plan check; Public Health Permit/License Application
applies_because: You prepare, serve or sell food

title: Seller's permit (California CDTFA)
summary: Businesses selling taxable goods register with the California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online at cdtfa.ca.gov: Register Online, then Register a New Business Activity; you can also register in person at a CDTFA office.
issuer: California Department of Tax and Fee Administration
fee: Confirm on CDTFA Publication 107 before stating (widely reported as no fee; a security deposit may be required)

title: Fictitious Business Name statement (LA County)
summary: If you do business under a name that is not your own legal name, you file a Fictitious Business Name statement with the LA County Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk. Open the County page for current fees, deadlines and the newspaper publication requirement.
fee: Not verified on the official page (secondary sources report $26 plus $5 per extra name or owner)
applies_because: You may operate under a business name different from your legal name

title: Register as an employer (California EDD)
summary: A business must register with the EDD within 15 days of paying more than $100 in wages in a calendar quarter. Register online through e-Services for Business. New hires must be reported within 20 calendar days of their first day of work.
documents: Business addresses, phone, email, date of first payroll over $100
deadlines: Register within 15 days of paying more than $100 in wages in a calendar quarter
Report each new hire within 20 calendar days of their first day
applies_because: You have, or plan to hire, employees

title: California minimum wage
summary: The statewide minimum wage is $16.90 per hour in 2026 and increases to $17.40 per hour on January 1, 2027, for all employers. Glendale's hotel worker wage is higher (see the hotel entry).
deadlines: Statewide minimum wage rises to $17.40 per hour on January 1, 2027
applies_because: You have, or plan to hire, employees

title: Hotel worker minimum wage (Glendale)
summary: Glendale hotel employers must pay at least $25.00 per hour from July 1, 2026. Annual CPI adjustments begin July 1, 2029.
applies_because: You operate a hotel in Glendale

title: Disposable foodware accessories only on request
summary: Food and beverage providers may not give utensils, napkins, straws and similar items unless the customer asks. Online and takeout orders must be opt-in. Drive-through and delivery staff may ask.
issuer: City of Glendale – Office of Sustainability

title: Polystyrene foodware ban
summary: No polystyrene foodware may be used, distributed or sold with prepared or raw food or beverages in Glendale. The rule also covers coolers, packing materials, egg cartons and meat, fish and produce trays. Non-polystyrene disposables are allowed.
issuer: City of Glendale – Office of Sustainability
applies_because: You serve or sell food or drinks

title: Business help from the City
summary: The Economic Development Division offers business assistance programs. Small business advising is available through the Small Business Development Center, and hiring help through the Verdugo Job Center.
